     3	module MPY-FUNCTIONS
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	
     6	  // call routing + callee/arg evaluation (#callee/#args/#argCont) live in call.k;
     7	  // this module owns the frame lifecycle (bind params, return, pop).
     8	  syntax KItem ::= frame(continuation: K, callerEnv: Int, savedLoc: Int)
     9	                 | #bindP(ParamNames, Vals)
    10	                 | "#pop"
    11	                 | "#endcall"
    12	
    13	  // ==== def / anonymous closure =============================================
    14	  rule <k> FuncDef(F:String, Params(PNS:ParamNames), BODY:Stmts) => .K ... </k>
    15	       <env> L:Int </env>
    16	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ F <- closureVal(PNS, BODY, L) ], _) ... </scopes>
    17	
    18	  syntax Expr ::= closureExpr(ParamNames, Stmts)
    19	  rule <k> closureExpr(PNS:ParamNames, BODY:Stmts) => closureVal(PNS, BODY, L) ... </k>
    20	       <env> L:Int </env>
    21	
    22	  // ==== annotated def/lambda (closure cells; spec 2.3) ======================
    23	  // closureValC(params, cellvars, body, captured-cells). No frame anchor: all
    24	  // enclosing-local reads are freevars (symtable-complete) and go through the
    25	  // captured cells; everything else is global/builtin, so the callee frame's
    26	  // parent is the module scope (0) — sound after the defining frame dies.
    27	  syntax Val ::= closureValC(ParamNames, ParamNames, Stmts, Map)
    28	
    29	  // capture: resolve each freevar to the enclosing frame's cellRef, then bind
    30	  // (FuncDef) or yield (Lambda) the closure value.
    31	  syntax KItem ::= #mkClosure(String, ParamNames, ParamNames, ParamNames, Stmts, Map)
    32	                 | #mkLambda(ParamNames, ParamNames, ParamNames, Stmts, Map)
    33	  rule <k> FuncDef(F:String, Params(PNS:ParamNames), CellVars(CVS:ParamNames),
    34	                   FreeVars(FVS:ParamNames), BODY:Stmts)
    35	        => #mkClosure(F, PNS, CVS, FVS, BODY, .Map) ... </k>
    36	  rule <k> #mkClosure(F:String, PNS:ParamNames, CVS:ParamNames,
    37	                      (FV:String, FVR:ParamNames), BODY:Stmts, CM:Map)
    38	        => #mkClosure(F, PNS, CVS, FVR, BODY, CM [ FV <- {M[FV]}:>Val ]) ... </k>
    39	       <env> L:Int </env>
    40	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
    41	       requires FV in_keys(M)
    42	  rule <k> #mkClosure(F:String, PNS:ParamNames, CVS:ParamNames,
    43	                      .ParamNames, BODY:Stmts, CM:Map) => .K ... </k>
    44	       <env> L:Int </env>
    45	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ F <- closureValC(PNS, CVS, BODY, CM) ], _) ... </scopes>
    46	
    47	  rule <k> Lambda(Params(PNS:ParamNames), E:Expr)
    48	        => closureVal(PNS, Return(E) .Stmts, L) ... </k>
    49	       <env> L:Int </env>
    50	  rule <k> Lambda(Params(PNS:ParamNames), CellVars(CVS:ParamNames),
    51	                  FreeVars(FVS:ParamNames), E:Expr)
    52	        => #mkLambda(PNS, CVS, FVS, Return(E) .Stmts, .Map) ... </k>
    53	  rule <k> #mkLambda(PNS:ParamNames, CVS:ParamNames,
    54	                     (FV:String, FVR:ParamNames), BODY:Stmts, CM:Map)
    55	        => #mkLambda(PNS, CVS, FVR, BODY, CM [ FV <- {M[FV]}:>Val ]) ... </k>
    56	       <env> L:Int </env>
    57	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
    58	       requires FV in_keys(M)
    59	  rule <k> #mkLambda(PNS:ParamNames, CVS:ParamNames, .ParamNames, BODY:Stmts, CM:Map)
    60	        => closureValC(PNS, CVS, BODY, CM) ... </k>
    61	
    62	  // ==== bind params ========================================================
    63	  rule <k> #bindP(.ParamNames, .Vals) => .K ... </k>
    64	  rule <k> #bindP((P:String, PS:ParamNames), (V:Val, VS:Vals)) => #bindP(PS, VS) ... </k>
    65	       <env> L:Int </env>
    66	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ P <- V ], _) ... </scopes>
    67	  // a param that is a cellvar was pre-bound to its cell at frame entry
    68	  rule <k> #bindP((P:String, PS:ParamNames), (V:Val, VS:Vals))
    69	        => #cellW({M[P]}:>Val, V) ~> #bindP(PS, VS) ... </k>
    70	       <env> L:Int </env>
    71	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
    72	       requires "$cells" in_keys(M)
    73	        andBool pnMember(P, cellsOf({M["$cells"]}:>Val))
    74	        andBool P in_keys(M) andBool isCellRef({M[P]}:>Val)
    75	       [priority(40)]
    76	
    77	  // ==== return / pop the frame (the returned expr evaluates by strictness) ==
    78	  rule <k> Return(V:Val) ~> _ => #pop </k>
    79	       <ret> noRet => retV(V) </ret>
    80	  rule <k> #endcall => #pop ... </k>
    81	       <ret> noRet => retV(noneV) </ret>
    82	  // pop: restore env, DEALLOCATE the callee frame, and wind scopeLoc back (LIFO allocation
    83	  // makes the saved loc the callee frame's own loc). Sound because no closureVal outlives its
    84	  // defining frame (frontend subset: no returned/stored closures; module defs live in loc 0).
    85	  rule <k> #pop => V ~> CONT </k>
    86	       <ret>   retV(V) => noRet </ret>
    87	       <stack> ListItem(frame(CONT:K, CALLERL:Int, SAVEDL:Int)) => .List ... </stack>
    88	       <env>   L:Int => CALLERL </env>
    89	       <scopes> SC:Map => SC [ L <- undef ] </scopes>
    90	       <scopeLoc> _ => SAVEDL </scopeLoc>
    91	endmodule
     1	// reference/src/semantics/subscript.k — MPY-SUBSCRIPT
     2	
     3	module MPY-SUBSCRIPT
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	
     6	  // ==== positional access + negative-index normalization (used only here) ===
     7	  // valSeqAt is [total]: in-bounds vCons access reduces as usual; on an OPAQUE sequence (e.g.
     8	  // a trusted sort's sortVS(VS)) or OOB it stays an abstract total value — so indexing the
     9	  // opaque sorted list is DEFINED (no undischarged #Ceil), matching the old semantics' total
    10	  // atK. K trusts the [total] annotation; valid programs index in-bounds.
    11	  syntax Val ::= valSeqAt(ValSeq, Int) [function, total]
    12	  rule valSeqAt(vCons(V:Val, _:ValSeq), 0)     => V
    13	  rule valSeqAt(vCons(_:Val, S:ValSeq), I:Int) => valSeqAt(S, I -Int 1)
    14	       requires I >Int 0
    15	
    16	  syntax Int ::= intSeqAt(IntSeq, Int) [function]
    17	  rule intSeqAt(iCons(C:Int, _:IntSeq), 0)     => C
    18	  rule intSeqAt(iCons(_:Int, S:IntSeq), I:Int) => intSeqAt(S, I -Int 1)
    19	       requires I >Int 0
    20	
    21	  syntax Int ::= normIdx(Int, Int) [function, total]
    22	  rule normIdx(I:Int, LEN:Int) => I +Int LEN requires I  <Int 0
    23	  rule normIdx(I:Int, _:Int)   => I          requires I >=Int 0
    24	
    25	  // ==== Subscript: indexing obj[i] (list / tuple / str) =====================
    26	  // contexts (not strict attrs): the Index slot's Slice alternative must never heat
    27	  context Subscript(HOLE, _)
    28	  context Subscript(_:Val, HOLE:Expr)
    29	
    30	  // heap-object deref (covers both the index and slice forms via the Index slot)
    31	  rule <k> Subscript(ref(H:Int), IX:Index) => Subscript(V, IX) ... </k>
    32	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    33	       [priority(40)]
    34	
    35	  rule <k> Subscript(OBJ:Val, I:Int) => applyIndex(OBJ, I) ... </k>
    36	
    37	  syntax Val ::= applyIndex(Val, Int) [function]
    38	  rule applyIndex(list(VS:ValSeq),  I:Int) => valSeqAt(VS, normIdx(I, vsLen(VS)))
    39	  rule applyIndex(tuple(VS:ValSeq), I:Int) => valSeqAt(VS, normIdx(I, vsLen(VS)))
    40	  rule applyIndex(str(IS:IntSeq),   I:Int)
    41	    => str(iCons(intSeqAt(IS, normIdx(I, isLen(IS))), .IntSeq))
    42	
    43	  // ==== Slice: obj[lo:hi:step] (list / str) — CPython slice.indices ==========
    44	  syntax KItem ::= #evalB(Bound) | "#toSome"
    45	                 | #slLo(Val, Bound, Bound)
    46	                 | #slHi(Val, OptInt, Bound)
    47	                 | #slStep(Val, OptInt, OptInt)
    48	
    49	  syntax OptInt ::= "noB" | someB(Int)
    50	  rule <k> #evalB(NoBound)  => noB ... </k>
    51	  rule <k> #evalB(E:Expr)   => E ~> #toSome ... </k>
    52	  rule <k> I:Int ~> #toSome => someB(I) ... </k>
    53	
    54	  rule <k> Subscript(OBJ:Val, Slice(LO:Bound, HI:Bound, ST:Bound)) => #evalB(LO) ~> #slLo(OBJ, HI, ST) ... </k>
    55	  rule <k> LO:OptInt ~> #slLo(OBJ:Val, HI:Bound, ST:Bound)   => #evalB(HI) ~> #slHi(OBJ, LO, ST) ... </k>
    56	  rule <k> HI:OptInt ~> #slHi(OBJ:Val, LO:OptInt, ST:Bound)  => #evalB(ST) ~> #slStep(OBJ, LO, HI) ... </k>
    57	  // a list slice constructs a NEW object; a str slice stays a value
    58	  rule <k> ST:OptInt ~> #slStep(list(VS:ValSeq), LO:OptInt, HI:OptInt)
    59	        => #alloc(doSlice(list(VS), LO, HI, ST)) ... </k>
    60	       [priority(45)]
    61	  rule <k> ST:OptInt ~> #slStep(OBJ:Val, LO:OptInt, HI:OptInt) => doSlice(OBJ, LO, HI, ST) ... </k>
    62	
    63	  syntax Val ::= doSlice(Val, OptInt, OptInt, OptInt) [function]
    64	  rule doSlice(list(VS:ValSeq), LO:OptInt, HI:OptInt, ST:OptInt)
    65	    => list(buildVS(VS, slStart(LO, ST, vsLen(VS)), slStop(HI, ST, vsLen(VS)), slStep(ST)))
    66	  rule doSlice(tuple(VS:ValSeq), LO:OptInt, HI:OptInt, ST:OptInt)
    67	    => tuple(buildVS(VS, slStart(LO, ST, vsLen(VS)), slStop(HI, ST, vsLen(VS)), slStep(ST)))
    68	  rule doSlice(str(IS:IntSeq), LO:OptInt, HI:OptInt, ST:OptInt)
    69	    => str(buildIS(IS, slStart(LO, ST, isLen(IS)), slStop(HI, ST, isLen(IS)), slStep(ST)))
    70	
    71	  // ==== slice.indices: step / start / stop / clamp ==========================
    72	  syntax Int ::= slStep(OptInt) [function, total]
    73	  rule slStep(noB)          => 1
    74	  rule slStep(someB(S:Int)) => S
    75	
    76	  syntax Int ::= slStart(OptInt, OptInt, Int) [function]
    77	  rule slStart(noB,          ST:OptInt, _LEN:Int) => 0
    78	       requires slStep(ST) >Int 0
    79	  rule slStart(noB,          ST:OptInt, LEN:Int)  => LEN -Int 1
    80	       requires slStep(ST) <Int 0
    81	  rule slStart(someB(I:Int), ST:OptInt, LEN:Int)  => slAdjust(I, LEN, slStep(ST))
    82	
    83	  syntax Int ::= slStop(OptInt, OptInt, Int) [function]
    84	  rule slStop(noB,          ST:OptInt, LEN:Int)  => LEN
    85	       requires slStep(ST) >Int 0
    86	  rule slStop(noB,          ST:OptInt, _LEN:Int) => -1
    87	       requires slStep(ST) <Int 0
    88	  rule slStop(someB(I:Int), ST:OptInt, LEN:Int)  => slAdjust(I, LEN, slStep(ST))
    89	
    90	  syntax Int ::= slAdjust(Int, Int, Int) [function, total]
    91	  rule slAdjust(I:Int, LEN:Int, STEP:Int) => clampLo(I +Int LEN, STEP)
    92	       requires I  <Int 0
    93	  rule slAdjust(I:Int, LEN:Int, STEP:Int) => clampHi(I, LEN, STEP)
    94	       requires I >=Int 0
    95	
    96	  syntax Int ::= clampLo(Int, Int) [function, total]
    97	  rule clampLo(J:Int, _STEP:Int) => J
    98	       requires J >=Int 0
    99	  rule clampLo(J:Int, STEP:Int)  => #if STEP <Int 0 #then -1 #else 0 #fi
   100	       requires J <Int 0
   101	
   102	  syntax Int ::= clampHi(Int, Int, Int) [function, total]
   103	  rule clampHi(I:Int, LEN:Int, _STEP:Int) => I
   104	       requires I  <Int LEN
   105	  rule clampHi(I:Int, LEN:Int, STEP:Int)  => #if STEP <Int 0 #then LEN -Int 1 #else LEN #fi
   106	       requires I >=Int LEN
   107	
   108	  // ==== build the strided sub-sequence (indices in range by construction) ====
   109	  syntax ValSeq ::= buildVS(ValSeq, Int, Int, Int) [function]
   110	  rule buildVS(VS:ValSeq, I:Int, STOP:Int, STEP:Int)
   111	    => vCons(valSeqAt(VS, I), buildVS(VS, I +Int STEP, STOP, STEP))
   112	       requires (STEP >Int 0 andBool I <Int STOP) orBool (STEP <Int 0 andBool I >Int STOP)
   113	  rule buildVS(_:ValSeq, I:Int, STOP:Int, STEP:Int) => .ValSeq
   114	       requires notBool ((STEP >Int 0 andBool I <Int STOP) orBool (STEP <Int 0 andBool I >Int STOP))
   115	
   116	  syntax IntSeq ::= buildIS(IntSeq, Int, Int, Int) [function]
   117	  rule buildIS(IS:IntSeq, I:Int, STOP:Int, STEP:Int)
   118	    => iCons(intSeqAt(IS, I), buildIS(IS, I +Int STEP, STOP, STEP))
   119	       requires (STEP >Int 0 andBool I <Int STOP) orBool (STEP <Int 0 andBool I >Int STOP)
   120	  rule buildIS(_:IntSeq, I:Int, STOP:Int, STEP:Int) => .IntSeq
   121	       requires notBool ((STEP >Int 0 andBool I <Int STOP) orBool (STEP <Int 0 andBool I >Int STOP))
   122	endmodule
     1	// reference/src/semantics/core.k — MPY-CORE
     2	
     3	module MPY-CORE
     4	  imports MPY-SYNTAX
     5	  imports INT
     6	  imports BOOL
     7	  imports STRING
     8	  imports MAP
     9	  imports LIST
    10	  imports K-EQUAL
    11	
    12	  // ==== values, the algebraic lists, and the scope heap =====================
    13	  syntax IntSeq ::= ".IntSeq" | iCons(Int, IntSeq)
    14	  syntax ValSeq ::= ".ValSeq" | vCons(Val, ValSeq)
    15	  syntax Str    ::= str(IntSeq)
    16	
    17	  // the iterable values, grouped under one sort (typing only — dispatch is <k>-cell)
    18	  syntax Iterable ::= list(ValSeq)
    19	                    | tuple(ValSeq)
    20	                    | Str
    21	                    | rangeObj(Int, Int, Int)
    22	                    | zipObj(ValSeq, ValSeq)
    23	                    | zipObjS(IntSeq, IntSeq)
    24	
    25	  syntax Val      ::= Int
    26	                    | Bool
    27	                    | "noneV"
    28	                    | Iterable
    29	                    | ref(Int)          // a heap object: <heap> holds its list(VS)
    30	                    | cellRef(Int)      // a closure cell: <heap> holds cellV(V)
    31	                    | closureVal(ParamNames, Stmts, Int)
    32	                    | typeV(String)     // a type object (int/str), resolved from the builtins frame
    33	                    | builtinV(String)  // a builtin function, resolved like any name (LEGB fallthrough)
    34	                    | boundMethodV(Val, String)   // a cooled Attribute: obj.method
    35	
    36	  syntax Parent   ::= "root" | parent(Int)
    37	  syntax Scope    ::= scope(Map, Parent)
    38	  syntax KResult  ::= Val
    39	  syntax Expr     ::= Val   // cooling puts results back into expression holes
    40	  syntax Vals     ::= List{Val, ","}
    41	  syntax Exc      ::= "NoExc" | "AssertionError"
    42	  syntax RetState ::= "noRet" | retV(Val)
    43	
    44	  // ==== configuration =======================================================
    45	  // The builtins namespace is a real scope at reserved location -1 (the bottom of every
    46	  // chain; scopeLoc only allocates >=1, so -1 never collides). The module scope (loc 0)
    47	  // has it as parent, so an unbound name resolves there last — exactly LEGB. `int`/`str`
    48	  // resolve to their type objects; any local/global binding shadows them via normal lookup.
    49	  configuration
    50	    <k>       #loadAll($PGM:Module) </k>
    51	    <env>     0 </env>
    52	    <scopes>   0     |-> scope(.Map, parent(-1))
    53	              -1    |-> builtinsScope </scopes>
    54	    <scopeLoc> 1 </scopeLoc>
    55	    <heap>    .Map </heap>
    56	    <heapLoc> 0 </heapLoc>
    57	    <stack>   .List </stack>
    58	    <ret>     noRet </ret>
    59	    <exc>     NoExc </exc>
    60	    <exit-code exit=""> 0 </exit-code>
    61	
    62	  // ==== heap allocation (constructed lists become objects) ==================
    63	  // Cons-form emission with a freshness guard (the heap-list-probe discipline:
    64	  // an update-form H[N <- _] never re-normalizes symbolically). heapLoc is
    65	  // monotonic — it does NOT wind back at #pop: returned lists escape by ref.
    66	  // A bare list(VS) Val stays legal (read-only inputs in claims flow unboxed);
    67	  // only CONSTRUCTORS in program syntax allocate.
    68	  syntax Bool ::= isRefV(Val) [function, total]
    69	  rule isRefV(ref(_:Int)) => true
    70	  rule isRefV(_:Val)      => false [owise]
    71	
    72	  // closure cells (Python-faithful capture): the heap holds cellV(V); a
    73	  // cellRef surfacing as the k-redex reads through (lookup is the only use —
    74	  // cellRefs never escape to user-visible values)
    75	  syntax HeapVal ::= cellV(Val)
    76	  syntax Bool ::= isCellRef(Val) [function, total]
    77	  rule isCellRef(cellRef(_:Int)) => true
    78	  rule isCellRef(_:Val)          => false [owise]
    79	  // k-top deref for cell-bound reads surfacing INSIDE the annotated frame
    80	  // (AugAssign's in-place read and friends). The "$cells" guard keeps this
    81	  // DECIDABLY inapplicable in plain frames — an unguarded rule lets the
    82	  // prover narrow abstract k-top values into cellRef junk (probed on
    83	  // 26-remove-duplicates). Cross-frame reads (a comprehension closure
    84	  // reading the enclosing function's cellvar) deref inside #look instead.
    85	  rule <k> cellRef(H:Int) => V ... </k>
    86	       <env> L:Int </env>
    87	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
    88	       <heap> ... H |-> cellV(V:Val) ... </heap>
    89	       requires "$cells" in_keys(M)
    90	       [priority(40)]
    91	
    92	  // write through a cell (Assign / #bindP / #bindTgt dispatch here on
    93	  // cell-bound names)
    94	  // a keyword argument cools to a TAGGED value (consumed by kw-aware builtins)
    95	  syntax Val ::= kwV(String, Val)
    96	  syntax KItem ::= #kwTag(String)
    97	  rule <k> KwArg(N:String, E:Expr) => E ~> #kwTag(N) ... </k>
    98	  rule <k> V:Val ~> #kwTag(N:String) => kwV(N, V) ... </k>
    99	       requires notBool isKwV(V)
   100	  syntax Bool ::= isKwV(Val) [function, total]
   101	  rule isKwV(kwV(_:String, _:Val)) => true
   102	  rule isKwV(_:Val)                => false [owise]
   103	
   104	  // the frame marker carries the CONCRETE cellvar list, so cell-write dispatch
   105	  // decides by pnMember even over an abstract frame rest (no prover branching)
   106	  syntax Val ::= cellsMark(ParamNames)
   107	  syntax ParamNames ::= cellsOf(Val) [function]
   108	  rule cellsOf(cellsMark(CVS:ParamNames)) => CVS

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+import json
+import re
+from pathlib import Path
+
+candidate_path = Path("/candidate/Proof.lean")
+candidate = candidate_path.read_text()
+target = json.loads(
+    Path("/reference/klean-generation/generator-manifest.json").read_text()
+)["target"]
+inventory = json.loads(Path("/reference/lemma-discovery.json").read_text())
+rule_class = {
+    rule["source_rule_id"]: rule["classification"]
+    for rule in inventory["rules"]
+}
+
+records = []
+for parameter in target["parameters"]:
+    name = parameter["name"]
+    pattern = re.compile(
+        r"(?m)^(?:noncomputable\s+)?def\s+"
+        + re.escape(name)
+        + r"(?=\s|\()"
+    )
+    matches = list(pattern.finditer(candidate))
+    definitions = []
+    for match in matches:
+        next_comment = candidate.find("\n/- KORE symbol:", match.end())
+        next_theorem = candidate.find("\n@[simp]", match.end())
+        ends = [end for end in (next_comment, next_theorem) if end >= 0]
+        end = min(ends) if ends else len(candidate)
+        definitions.append(
+            {
+                "start_line": candidate.count("\n", 0, match.start()) + 1,
+                "text": candidate[match.start() : end].rstrip(),
+            }
+        )
+    records.append(
+        {
+            **parameter,
+            "candidate_definition_count": len(matches),
+            "candidate_definitions": definitions,
+            "source_classifications": [
+                rule_class[source_rule_id]
+                for source_rule_id in parameter["source_rule_ids"]
+            ],
+        }
+    )
+
+print(
+    json.dumps(
+        {
+            "candidate": str(candidate_path),
+            "parameter_count": len(target["parameters"]),
+            "all_parameters_have_exactly_one_candidate_definition": all(
+                record["candidate_definition_count"] == 1
+                for record in records
+            ),
+            "parameters": records,
+        },
+        indent=2,
+        sort_keys=True,
+    )
+)
*** End Patch

<permissions instructions>
Filesystem sandboxing defines which files can be read or written. `sandbox_mode` is `workspace-write`: The sandbox permits reading files, and editing files in `cwd` and `writable_roots`. Editing files in other directories requires approval. Network access is restricted.
Approval policy is currently never. Do not provide the `sandbox_permissions` for any reason, commands will be rejected.
 The writable roots are `/audit-output`, `/tmp`, `/tmp/audit-work`.
</permissions instructions>

<skills_instructions>
## Skills
A skill is a set of instructions provided through a `SKILL.md` source. Below is the list of skills that can be used. Each entry includes a name, description, and source locator. `file` locators are on the host filesystem, `environment resource` locators are owned by an execution environment, `orchestrator resource` locators are opaque non-filesystem resources, and `custom resource` locators use their provider's access mechanism.
### Available skills
- imagegen: Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. Do not use when the task is better handled by editing existing SVG/vector/code-native assets, extending an established icon or logo system, or building the visual directly in HTML/CSS/canvas. (file: /home/agent/.audit-supervisor.hszWeU/codex-home/skills/.system/imagegen/SKILL.md)
- openai-docs: Use when the user asks how to build with OpenAI products or APIs, asks about Codex itself or choosing Codex surfaces, needs up-to-date official documentation with citations, help choosing the latest model for a use case, or model upgrade and prompt-upgrade guidance; use OpenAI docs MCP tools for non-Codex docs questions, use the Codex manual helper first for broad Codex self-knowledge, and restrict fallback browsing to official OpenAI domains. (file: /home/agent/.audit-supervisor.hszWeU/codex-home/skills/.system/openai-docs/SKILL.md)
- plugin-creator: Create and scaffold plugin directories for Codex with a required `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, optional plugin folders/files, valid manifest defaults, and personal-marketplace entries by default. Use when Codex needs to create a new personal plugin, add optional plugin structure, generate or update marketplace entries for plugin ordering and availability metadata, or update an existing local plugin during development with the CLI-driven cachebuster and reinstall flow. (file: /home/agent/.audit-supervisor.hszWeU/codex-home/skills/.system/plugin-creator/SKILL.md)
- skill-creator: Guide for creating effective skills. This skill should be used when users want to create a new skill (or update an existing skill) that extends Codex's capabilities with specialized knowledge, workflows, or tool integrations. (file: /home/agent/.audit-supervisor.hszWeU/codex-home/skills/.system/skill-creator/SKILL.md)
- skill-installer: Install Codex skills into $CODEX_HOME/skills from a curated list or a GitHub repo path. Use when a user asks to list installable skills, install a curated skill, or install a skill from another repo (including private repos). (file: /home/agent/.audit-supervisor.hszWeU/codex-home/skills/.system/skill-installer/SKILL.md)
- k-proof-technique: Use when constructing a K reachability proof requires deriving a loop invariant, choosing a summary representation, laying out proof obligations, or abstracting an operation kprove cannot evaluate. (file: /home/agent/.audit-supervisor.hszWeU/codex-home/skills/k-proof-technique/SKILL.md)
- proving-spec: Use when a K spec does not pass kprove yet — the proof hangs, diverges, prints WarnStuckClaimState, or exits non-zero — and you need to make it pass. (file: /home/agent/.audit-supervisor.hszWeU/codex-home/skills/proving-spec/SKILL.md)
- reasoning-on-paper: Use when the user explicitly requests an on-paper K proof, or live K tooling cannot be made available and the user accepts an unchecked fallback. (file: /home/agent/.audit-supervisor.hszWeU/codex-home/skills/reasoning-on-paper/SKILL.md)

Apps (Connectors) can be explicitly triggered in user messages in the format `[$app-name](app://{connector_id})`. Apps can also be implicitly triggered as long as the context suggests usage of available apps.
An app is equivalent to a set of MCP tools within the `codex_apps` MCP.
An installed app's MCP tools are either provided to you already, or can be lazy-loaded through the `tool_search` tool. If `tool_search` is available, the apps that are searchable by `tools_search` will be listed by it.
Do not additionally call list_mcp_resources or list_mcp_resource_templates for apps.
</apps_instructions>

You are `/root`, the primary agent in a team of agents collaborating to fulfill the user's goals.

At the start of your turn, you are the active agent.
You can spawn sub-agents to handle subtasks, and those sub-agents can spawn their own sub-agents.
All agents in the team, including the agents that you can assign tasks to, are equally intelligent and capable, and have access to the same set of tools.

You can use `spawn_agent` to create a new agent, `followup_task` to give an existing agent a new task and trigger a turn, and `send_message` to pass a message to a running agent without triggering a turn.
Child agents can also spawn their own sub-agents.
You can decide how much context you want to propagate to your sub-agents with the `fork_turns` parameter.

You will receive messages in the analysis channel in the form:
```
Message Type: MESSAGE | FINAL_ANSWER
Task name: <recipient>
Sender: <author>
Payload:
<payload text>
```
They may be addressed as to=/root

Note that collaboration tools cannot be called from inside `functions.exec`. Call `spawn_agent`, `send_message`, `followup_task`, `wait_agent`, `interrupt_agent`, and `list_agents` only as direct tool calls using the recipient shown in their tool definitions, such as `to=functions.collaboration.spawn_agent`, since they are intentionally absent from the `functions.exec` `tools.*` namespace. Available tools in `functions.exec` are explicitly described with a `tools` namespace in the developer message.

All agents share the same directory. In detail:
- All agents have access to the same container and filesystem as you.
- All agents use the same current working directory.
- As a result, edits made by one agent are immediately visible to all other agents.

There are 4 available concurrency slots, meaning that up to 4 agents can be active at once, including you.

import json
import re
from pathlib import Path

candidate_path = Path("/candidate/Proof.lean")
candidate = candidate_path.read_text()
target = json.loads(
    Path("/reference/klean-generation/generator-manifest.json").read_text()
)["target"]
inventory = json.loads(Path("/reference/lemma-discovery.json").read_text())
rule_class = {
    rule["source_rule_id"]: rule["classification"]
    for rule in inventory["rules"]
}

records = []
for parameter in target["parameters"]:
    name = parameter["name"]
    pattern = re.compile(
        r"(?m)^(?:noncomputable\s+)?def\s+"
        + re.escape(name)
        + r"(?=\s|\()"
    )
    matches = list(pattern.finditer(candidate))
    definitions = []
    for match in matches:
        next_comment = candidate.find("\n/- KORE symbol:", match.end())
        next_theorem = candidate.find("\n@[simp]", match.end())
        ends = [end for end in (next_comment, next_theorem) if end >= 0]
        end = min(ends) if ends else len(candidate)
        definitions.append(
            {
                "start_line": candidate.count("\n", 0, match.start()) + 1,
                "text": candidate[match.start() : end].rstrip(),
            }
        )
    records.append(
        {
            **parameter,
            "candidate_definition_count": len(matches),
            "candidate_definitions": definitions,
            "source_classifications": [
                rule_class[source_rule_id]
                for source_rule_id in parameter["source_rule_ids"]
            ],
        }
    )

print(
    json.dumps(
        {
            "candidate": str(candidate_path),
            "parameter_count": len(target["parameters"]),
            "all_parameters_have_exactly_one_candidate_definition": all(
                record["candidate_definition_count"] == 1
                for record in records
            ),
            "parameters": records,
        },
        indent=2,
        sort_keys=True,
    )
)

[`29-operational-bridge-examples-corrected.log`](/audit-output/evidence/29-operational-bridge-examples-corrected.log).
The scalar and sequence definitions are substantive, and the list-backed map
definitions are plausible locally. Nevertheless, a collection of locally
plausible operations cannot bridge an omitted source datatype. The decisive
counterfactual shows that the theorem places no semantic constraint at all on
the Scope update/deletion behavior.

## Conclusion

Stage 3 passes independent classification and bijection review. Stage 4
passes producer provenance and deterministic structural checks, and Stage 5
passes clean-build, target-identity, lexical trust, and axiom-accounting
checks. The overall result nevertheless fails because the generated target
replaces an inhabited operational K sort with an empty Lean sort, making two
required domain lemmas vacuous. `Proof.final` therefore does not prove the
fresh-scope update and deletion facts for the frozen supplied semantics.

The raw command ledger is
[`COMMANDS.md`](/audit-output/evidence/COMMANDS.md).
